Classification of Surfaces

Chapter 8 of The Symmetries of Things, to play with

A zipper is a pair of arrows to be glued, tail to tail and head to head. Zip the rim of one hole, or of two: only four things can happen. p. 93

A tidy surface is a sphere with holes, handles, crosscaps and cross-handles. Only how many of each matters. p. 96

Every surface is polygons and zippers. Zip one pair at a time: what you hold stays tidy (a sphere with holes, handles, crosscaps, cross-handles), so it ends tidy. p. 97

To name a surface, count three things: its Euler characteristic, its boundaries, its sides. p. 105

    So it is

    The two halves of the rim are mirror images, so the hole just closes. A cap adds nothing. p. 94

    Each rim point is glued to the one opposite. The sheet has to pass through itself. p. 94

    Two tubes grow out of the same side and meet. p. 95

    One tube grows out, the other in. They meet through the sheet, front against back. p. 95

    Add pieces with the + buttons. Where a piece sits does not matter: push it anywhere and it is the same surface. p. 96

    Beside a crosscap a handle is a cross-handle: take one of its holes for a walk through the crosscap and it comes back reversed. So . p. 102

    Why only four

    A zipper pairs two arrows. They sit on one rim or on two, and they run opposite ways round or the same way. That is two choices twice. The colours show the paper's two sides: where teal meets sand along a seam, the surface has become one-sided.

    The three numbers

    Draw any map on a surface: its Euler characteristic is vertices minus edges plus faces, whatever the map. A sphere has . A hole or a crosscap lowers by 1, a handle or a cross-handle by 2: for handles, holes, crosscaps, cross-handles. p. 103

    After the trades, is two-sided with , and is one-sided with . Two different symbols differ in sides, boundaries or , so they are different surfaces. p. 102

    Why the book needs this

    Fold a repeating pattern up and you get its orbifold: one of these surfaces, with cone points inside and corner points on its boundaries. So the symbols , and are all a signature can hold besides its numbers: wonders, kaleidoscopes and miracles. p. 102

    What you are doing

    A polygon is a disc, and a disc is a sphere with a hole. That is where every piece starts: tidy. p. 97

    A zip joins two rims, or two stretches of one rim, and its two arrows run opposite ways round or the same way. Whatever rim is not zipped stays a hole: the book calls that case gaping, and the case with nothing left snug. p. 97

    After each zip the picture is redrawn with every piece in a place of its own. Nothing is lost by that. p. 96
